q: A farmer is standing on a riverbank with a fox, a chicken, and a bag of grain. He has a large boat that can carry himself and all three of the items together in a single trip. What is the minimum number of boat trips across the river he needs to get himself and all three items to the other side?
gold: 1 trip (the boat holds everything, so he crosses once)
resp:
# River Crossing Solution

The minimum number of trips is **1**.

Since the boat is large enough to carry the farmer plus all three items (fox, chicken, and grain) together, he can simply load everything into the boat and cross in a single trip.

---

**Note:** This differs from the classic "farmer, fox, chicken, and grain" puzzle, where the boat can only carry the farmer plus one other item. In that version, the answer is 7 trips because of the constraints that the fox can't be left alone with the chicken, and the chicken can't be left alone with the grain.
